utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And did that house look like it had been burned?

utterances.speaker: SUHRA SINANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I'm finished with that exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: If the witness can now be shown Defence Exhibit D96, which I'm afraid we mistakenly noted at P96 at one point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, and don't worry about it. This is the photo of a certain person.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes, indeed.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Do you recognise the person in this photograph, Ms. Sinanovic?

utterances.speaker: SUHRA SINANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Who is it?

utterances.speaker: SUHRA SINANOVIC
utterances.text: Novo Ilic.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And is that -- is that the same Novo Ilic, the son of Cvijeta Ilic who you described earlier or is it a different Novo Ilic?

utterances.speaker: SUHRA SINANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, the same Novo Ilic, the son of Cvijeta.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I'm done with that exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I'm going to end by showing you a few documents. The first is entitled a criminal report against Alija Izetbegovic, Sefer Halilovic, and Naser Oric, and the B/C/S is 00632970, that's the front page of the English. And returning to page 00633091 in B/C/S. And in the English it's -- well, it's the last two pages of our -- of this hand-out. Now -- right. I'm just going to ask you to look at page, as I said in the B/C/S it's 3091 and find your name, Suhra Sinanovic, Bjelovac, Bratunac, and it says in English: "Active participant in majority of attacks on Serb villages, organiser of plundering and destruction of family homes, Filipovic, Matic, Stojanovic, and Petrovic. From Serb villages, Bjelovac, Loznicka Rijeka, and Sikiric." Now, my question is: Is this -- were you an active participant in attacks on Serb villages?

utterances.speaker: SUHRA SINANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Were you an organiser of the plundering and destruction of the property of the Filipovic, Matic, Stojanovic, and Petrovic families?

utterances.speaker: SUHRA SINANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Do you know whether your property was in fact looted by Serbs at any stage?

utterances.speaker: SUHRA SINANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. When I talked to Mira Filipovic she told me that Rosa Ilic had taken all my property to Serbia. And naturally, afterwards, when Slavoljub Filipovic established a cafe there, they destroyed all of my property and then accused me of doing that. However, they were the ones who did that.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I would just ask for an exhibit number for this document, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. This would become Defence Exhibit 75 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: 754. 754. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you. And we have another two documents the next one is ERN 00678865 to 00678878, and the English is 00850546 to 00850560, and the top of the title is "Organisers of Genocide against the Serbian people."

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And if we turn to page 14 in the English, 00850559, and in the B/C/S it's 00678878, we again see your name. Without going detail I'll just ask you: Are you an organiser of the genocide against the Serbian people?

utterances.speaker: SUHRA SINANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I'll just ask for the exhibit number for this document, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. This will become Defence Exhibit D755. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And then lastly I have a document with ERN 01334640, and this is -- sorry 01 -- yes. I'll give the ERN for the B/C/S 00799571 to 00799578. And this purports to be a list of war criminals known to the command of the 1st light infantry brigade who committed war crimes in the area of Bratunac, Srebrenica, Milici, Vlasenica, and Skelani municipalities and are believed to be in Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I just want to ask you about some of the names on this list and if you can tell us what, if anything, you know about their movements in 1992. First of all, number 15, Dzevad Gusic.

utterances.speaker: SUHRA SINANOVIC
utterances.text: In Tuzla, in 1992 in April, he went to Tuzla then.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Number 16, Izet Gusic?

utterances.speaker: SUHRA SINANOVIC
utterances.text: He was in Slovenia in April of 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Number 120, if you can find that, Zihnija Sinanovic, do you know where he or she was?

utterances.speaker: SUHRA SINANOVIC
utterances.text: He was in Macedonia from 1993 until 2001.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Let's look at 169, Mujo Becirovic -- actually, no, I believe 167, Mehmedalija Begzadic?

utterances.speaker: SUHRA SINANOVIC
utterances.text: He was in Tuzla.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Finally let's look at 235, the name Mirsad Malagic. Do you know anything about him?

utterances.speaker: SUHRA SINANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. In the beginning of 1992 he was killed by a shell.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And your name appears at number 326. I just note that for the record and I won't ask you any questions in that record.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I'll just ask for an exhibit number, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So this will become Defence Exhibit D756, Mr. Jones.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Is there a mistake in the transcript?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes. I think for Mirsad Malagic the witness might have said what month he left.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: In what month did Mirsad Malagic leave -- my apologies, killed by a shell?

utterances.speaker: SUHRA SINANOVIC
utterances.text: Mirsad Malagic was killed in May in the very beginning -- or rather, mid-May. When the first shelling started he was killed by the shells then.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: All right. Now, a different subject. Do you know Fatima Hasanovic?

utterances.speaker: SUHRA SINANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Did you see her when you were in Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: SUHRA SINANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I saw her in 1994 when she came from Loznica from Serbia, because she had been wounded and transferred to Serbia, where she stayed for about a year and a half.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Did she tell you any story involving Slavka Matic?

utterances.speaker: SUHRA SINANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Just tell us briefly what she told you.

utterances.speaker: SUHRA SINANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, when she came, thousands of families went to see that woman after all that time had passed. She told everyone that she had been wounded and taken to Loznica, to Serbia, to hospital there. She was wounded in her hip. And, as they were unable to operate on her in Loznica, her doctor made arrangements for her to be operated in the Koviljaca spa. So she was taken to that spa, and upon her arrival there she saw Slavka Matic, Grozda Matic, and Cvjetko Lukic. These patients from the hospital created a disorder claiming that Muslims should not be operated in that hospital. Slavka allegedly said that if doctors operate on her she would set fire to the hospital; that was her revenge. She was there, Slavka was there, and she was saying that no Muslims could be operated upon in Koviljaca spa.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, two items on the transcript. When the witness was speaking, she said that Fatima spent a year and a half in a camp in Serbia. So the word "camp" is missing from the transcript. And then in the transcript it is also stated "Slavka allegedly said"; that's not what the witness said. She didn't say "Slavka allegedly said." She simply said she heard from Fatima that Slavka had said. So I just wanted this to be clarified.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When Fatima was brought to Koviljaca spa, or Banja Koviljaca, she found Slavka Matic, Grozda Matic and Cvjetko, and many other patients who did not allow a Muslim to be operated upon in Banja Koviljaca. And Fatima told me that Slavka had said that if they did operate on her in Banja Koviljaca that she would set fire to the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes, in other words if the doctors operated on Fatima, Slavka would set fire to the hospital. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SUHRA SINANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Is Fatima Hasanovic still living?

utterances.speaker: SUHRA SINANOVIC
utterances.text: No. Fatima was alive until several years ago. This is why she died, because when she came to Tuzla and Sarajevo it was too late. They operated on her several times, and after that she died.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Now, one question on the time when you were in Srebrenica. You were in Srebrenica in 1992/1993. Correct -- and, in fact, beyond?

utterances.speaker: SUHRA SINANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: In the period before demilitarisation, were you aware at any stage of a curfew being organised?

utterances.speaker: SUHRA SINANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: In your view, would it have been possible to have a curfew based on what you saw and experienced in Srebrenica at that time?

utterances.speaker: SUHRA SINANOVIC
utterances.text: No. As far as I know there was no police at all there.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: But why do you say it wouldn't have been possible to have a curfew?

utterances.speaker: SUHRA SINANOVIC
utterances.text: Because in Srebrenica there were 50.000 refugees and there was no police whatsoever. So this is the first time I hear of a curfew.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And finally, and slightly going back to these photographs we saw earlier but a point I should clarify, you saw these photographs and I asked you about what you saw in Bjelovac on the 20th or 21st of December, 1992, when you were there. Did you see at that time any houses that looked like they'd been burnt, like they'd been set fire to?

utterances.speaker: SUHRA SINANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And I'm excluding from that the Mujic, Lolic houses which you said had been burnt in May 1992, if that was clear.

utterances.speaker: SUHRA SINANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes, no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Mr. Jones. Now, how much time do you require, Mr. Wubben?

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: 25 minutes, half an hour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, certainly.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Half an hour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We'll have a 30-minute break, and then I take it that you will go till the very end and you finish?

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So now, Madam Sinanovic, Mr. Wubben, who is lead counsel for the Prosecution in this case, will be cross-examining you. Hopefully we will be finished today.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I'm confident we will finish today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Good morning -- good afternoon. My name is Jan Wubben. I am lead counsel for the Prosecution, as stated by Presiding Judge, and I will pose questions to you. Will you please give me a short answer when possible. And if any question by me is unclear, please ask me for clarification. And if you don't know, please state you don't. Yes?

utterances.speaker: SUHRA SINANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: In your statement this morning you testified about your times in Bjelovac and the developments there shortly after the war started. Did you notice in Bjelovac at that time, let me say April or earlier, March, or some later, any set of village guards?

utterances.speaker: SUHRA SINANOVIC
utterances.text: By the end of April, in April generally, when I first started seeing uniformed soldiers and when I went to Cvijeta's house and when I met Novo Ilic and Slavoljub Filipovic, that is when they went to guard duty and they were uniformed. And Novo's mother, Cvijeta, did say that -- she said we would go somewhere else to give them time to go out of the house and go and do their guard duty.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: So -- so it is a fact that in Bjelovac at that time guard duties had been organised?

utterances.speaker: SUHRA SINANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: And were these duties organised by the Serbs, or mixed by the Serbs and the Muslims, or the Muslims?

utterances.speaker: SUHRA SINANOVIC
utterances.text: No. It was only organised for Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Do you also know the reason why this was all organised and set; up?

utterances.speaker: SUHRA SINANOVIC
utterances.text: I wouldn't be able to tell you as to why they organised that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Did you happen to ask any of the known village guards to you why they were acting like that or ...

utterances.speaker: SUHRA SINANOVIC
utterances.text: I wasn't able to ask that question because of fear. I was frightened. I was even too scared to go out into my own backyard or walk down the street. We had to hide and stay indoors and try and be as inconspicuous as possible. Because we were Muslims we didn't want to be seen. They used to walk around during the day as well. They were uniformed and they walked around Bjelovac, but I didn't know any of these people.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: But what was the reason they were guarding for? Were they afraid? Were they being threatened?

utterances.speaker: SUHRA SINANOVIC
utterances.text: No, they were not threatened by anyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Did they fear an attack from outside towards Bjelovac?

utterances.speaker: SUHRA SINANOVIC
utterances.text: I'm unable to tell you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Did they build any trenches around Bjelovac or in Bjelovac?

utterances.speaker: SUHRA SINANOVIC
utterances.text: Up until the 11th of May, as long as I stayed there, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: And after the 11th of May?

utterances.speaker: SUHRA SINANOVIC
utterances.text: I wasn't there after the 11th of May. I wasn't in Bjelovac.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: You don't know?

utterances.speaker: SUHRA SINANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: But you arrived afterwards -- but I return to that issue later. In -- you told the Court that you went to Srebrenica, stayed there. And on the 13th of December, 1992, in the afternoon you went towards Bjelovac. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SUHRA SINANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I went to Poloznik.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Now, what make you leave on that particular day, on the 13th of December, towards that village that you mentioned?

utterances.speaker: SUHRA SINANOVIC
utterances.text: Because the day before nine members of my family who were living in Srebrenica with other refugees, there were 20 of us in that flat, and we had nothing to eat. And I couldn't bear to look at my children starving, and I had to do something, bring back some food, or the other option was to watch my children starve to death.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: So what did you discuss then as an opportunity for them?

utterances.speaker: SUHRA SINANOVIC
utterances.text: Either to go get food or to watch my children die of starvation.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: But what makes you choose to go for food with such a large number of people, as you stated?

utterances.speaker: SUHRA SINANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, when you see one, two, three people setting out, that was a kind of sign and it was only normal for people to go together. So as soon as we saw anyone setting out -- well, people were dying of hunger, as I said, and it was an imposed choice, as it were. And there were thousands of people setting out to get food. Some people would come back alive, others wouldn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Is it your testimony that you didn't knew that you would go to Bjelovac or Poloznik when you left on the 13th of December?

utterances.speaker: SUHRA SINANOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't know exactly that I was going to go there, but my neighbour, one of my neighbours, said they were going and she set out. And I said we had nothing left to eat, and I had to do something. And then she said, Let's go in the direction of Poloznik, and we saw a column of people, thousands of civilians, looking for food.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Wasn't it known at the time that an operation or an action was set up towards Bjelovac?

utterances.speaker: SUHRA SINANOVIC
utterances.text: As wife and mother, I had responsibilities for my own family and I took care of my own children and I knew nothing about anything of the sort. I was fighting for the sheer survival of my children and my family.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Didn't you learn any rumours around the 13th of December in the afternoon or some earlier that an action would be set up towards the Bjelovac area?

utterances.speaker: SUHRA SINANOVIC
utterances.text: I said that I heard from my neighbour because I was telling her I had nothing to eat, and she said to me, Let's go in the direction of Poloznik. And that's how I started on the way to Poloznik, with her and with the other people, because we were starving.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: So you decide to go to Poloznik because this woman told you so Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. that it would be an opportunity and you didn't wonder how to prepare in what for and whether the information is sure to get food over there?

utterances.speaker: SUHRA SINANOVIC
utterances.text: We knew that there was still people living in Poloznik. There were people there, and I was hoping that some of my relatives would be able to give me some food. So that was my intention when I set out in the direction of Poloznik, in order to ask them for some food. And so I stayed there overnight, and the next day I went on to Bjelovac and I didn't even get halfway there --

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Thank you. I will get to that issue later on, but I have a question regarding those people joining you. You told the Court there were thousands of people joining you in this journey towards the direction that ends up for you in Poloznik. Those people, did you talk to those people that were accompanying you?

utterances.speaker: SUHRA SINANOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't know any of those other people. I only talked to this neighbour of mine about how we could make ends meet and whether we would be able to bring anything back to our children and whether when we got back the next day they would still be alive or they will have died of hunger already.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Did you learn from any one of those people also undertaking that journey that Bjelovac might be an operation for food, for getting food? Sorry.

utterances.speaker: SUHRA SINANOVIC
utterances.text: I've told you that I went in the direction of Poloznik and I kept discussing these things -- I mean food-related issues with my neighbour; and as to any operation, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Didn't you wonder whether or not all those thousands of people would go to that village of Poloznik or have -- might have another reason to undertake that journey as well?

utterances.speaker: SUHRA SINANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, not all of us went to Poloznik because there were other villages in the surrounding areas such as Lokve and Brezovica, and if people had friends there in those other villages they went there. Not everybody went to Poloznik.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: So -- sorry. So therefore it's pure coincidence that you went to Poloznik on the same day as thousands of others went to other villages?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Just one moment. Yes, Mr. Jones.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I don't see what the coincidence is supposed to be. It's simply that, people going to different places. Where's the coincidence?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, you are right.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I -- with all respect, I disagree. The coincidence is that there are a lot of villages --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, you need to rephrase your question. I men, you are assuming and giving to the witness the conclusion, nothing but the conclusion, that this was pure coincidence. And you are asking her to explain.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Okay, I will rephrase.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You shouldn't put to the witness that it is definitely pure coincidence; let her explain how on the same day in the same place there were several thousand of people, some going one direction and others going in another direction and she will explain why if she knows why. But you put in her mouth -- that's why I let Mr. Jones go ahead with his objection. You were not suggesting, you were leaving no alternative that it was pure coincidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: I will rephrase, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Do you have an explanation why so many people, thousands of people, were aiming on the same day, the same afternoon, for such a journey which ends up in various directions, various villages, as you stated?

utterances.speaker: SUHRA SINANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I've told you that we were going hungry. We simply had to find some means of survival, that is to say food. And it was indeed a coincidence that I joined all these other people on the way in their search for food together with my neighbourhood. Because I've told you, we did not all go to Poloznik. People had friends and relations in different villages. I can't tell you now exactly how many villages there are in the area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Again, we have -- I understand of course the answer that you have given, but there is one point which you haven't explained. Why exactly this was happening on the 13th? Did it happen the day before? Or the day before? Why was it all happening on the 13th of December? This is what Mr. Wubben wants you to explain, if you have an explanation. Because if you don't, then obviously you tell us "I don't know."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I said that a couple of days before setting off we had nothing to eat. And so I had to go somewhere, no matter where. I just had to find some food for my child. I didn't know how to tell my 2-year-old child that I had no food, and I couldn't simply sit back and watch them suffer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Wubben.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: While you were joining this group of thousands taking this route, those people, were they all civilians or were there also fighters or soldiers accompanying the group?

utterances.speaker: SUHRA SINANOVIC
utterances.text: Those are civilians only.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Only civilians. The civilians including you were undertaking quite a long distance for travel, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: SUHRA SINANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it was a long way away.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Were you by any chance secured from any threats from the outside world, or I'd like to say mines, or ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think -- do you understand the question?

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: If you don't understand the question, you should confirm so and I will rephrase.

utterances.speaker: SUHRA SINANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you just repeat it, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: I will repeat the question. When you undertake --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I would suggest, Mr. Wubben, if you could rephrase it a little bit. You are in cross-examination, so you can go direct and explain exactly what -- what you mean. Because it will be easier for the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: As you were all civilians, you should -- you were afraid, isn't it, because it was wartime?

utterances.speaker: SUHRA SINANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: And because you were afraid and planned to undertake such a long journey, you should be secured at the utmost, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: SUHRA SINANOVIC
utterances.text: We had no security whatsoever. We just set off no matter in what direction, simply to find some means of survival.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Now, you were aiming for Serb-held territory, or at least in the neighbourhood. So weren't you concerned about meeting any Serb forces, soldiers, who would be hostile?

utterances.speaker: SUHRA SINANOVIC
utterances.text: I did say, we didn't really care. I just had to get food, and it was better to get killed rather than come back empty-handed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: One moment, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, whilst Mr. Wubben is pondering this I would like to make a correction for the transcript. The witness had said "I had to get food and it was better for me to get killed rather than for my family to starve and not to come back empty-handed." Could the witness please confirm this, rather than "for my family to die of starvation."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, okay. Let's -- whenever you're ready, Mr. Wubben.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: So it is your testimony that these group of thousands of people went to Serb-held territory or the neighbourhood of it, feared hostile encountering with Serb soldiers or forces, but didn't at all organise any guards to secure them?

utterances.speaker: SUHRA SINANOVIC
utterances.text: I did not say that we were afraid. I said that we were driven by hunger. That's why we had to go. It was better to get hit by a bullet, to step on a land-mine, rather than to have to watch your family slowly dying of starvation in your own house.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. She hasn't answered the question as yet. But yes, Mr. Jones.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, this witness has been giving evidence obviously about what she -- was going through her mind and whether she was organising anything and concerned for her security. For her to be asked questions about what the thousands of people were doing and what was passing through their minds and why they were going to territories, I think, is unfair on her. Because if she answers it, then she'll be speaking on behalf of thousands of people and that's obviously -- I mean, she can't do -- she can speak for herself, but not for what thousands of people --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think that she knows that she can only speak for herself.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And, also, Poloznik is not Serb-held territory. She's given evidence that it was -- that there were Bosniaks there, so it's one thing to say that they were nearby Serb territory but it's not that she's going right into Serb territory.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And that's marginal, Mr. Jones, because they had to pass through certain territories that -- I better not mention anything else. Yes. Mr. Wubben, she hasn't answered your question, the essence of which was actually whether she is aware of any arrangements that were in place to have protection while they were on the road to wherever they were heading, protection by means of either guarded soldiers or guards or whatever.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: The question is, Witness: Were you aware of any such arrangements for protection of the group of civilians?

utterances.speaker: SUHRA SINANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: And during that journey you learned from no one about any action, any planned action or operation, on Bjelovac?

utterances.speaker: SUHRA SINANOVIC
utterances.text: No. I told you last time that I had no contact with anyone but my neighbour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Now, after your arrival in Poloznik, you tried to get to Bjelovac. Isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: SUHRA SINANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: And that was the 14th of December, if I recall correctly?

utterances.speaker: SUHRA SINANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: And can you tell me about the circumstances of that trip, because you already reiterated in beginning this afternoon that you only came halfway.

utterances.speaker: SUHRA SINANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I only managed to get halfway there to Poloznik. I came to Loznicka Rijeka, which is halfway.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: What made you stop?

utterances.speaker: SUHRA SINANOVIC
utterances.text: We were stopped by the numerous shells and the aviation -- the planes that flew above us constantly.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: And did you try to wait and to move on forwards Bjelovac, as aimed?

utterances.speaker: SUHRA SINANOVIC
utterances.text: For some five to ten minutes only when the shelling started, we started withdrawing towards Poloznik hiding under the trees, going from one tree to the next one. And this is how we were protecting ourselves from the shells and the aviation.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: But I take it then that the whole group hide for the shelling -- or how many -- by the way, I will rephrase the question. How big was the group? How many people were there aiming for Bjelovac with you?

utterances.speaker: SUHRA SINANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you mean the 14th?

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: SUHRA SINANOVIC
utterances.text: It was a large group. And whoever was able to find shelter under the tree, did that. Others just stood on the goat path expecting to be hit and killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: And can you give a number in that respect? Hundreds? Hundreds of people in that group?

utterances.speaker: SUHRA SINANOVIC
utterances.text: Thousands, not hundreds.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: And I don't recall that I put that question to you, so why specific Bjelovac? Was that because of you living there before?

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: I recall that she told something about getting properties in --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yeah --

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: -- her house.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Because she said she left a lot of food in her house.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: So I withdraw that question, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: And next question is: So you were hiding from the shelling and what did you do after that, after you hide?

utterances.speaker: SUHRA SINANOVIC
utterances.text: After that, as I said, we went from one tree to the next one trying to find shelter from the shells and the aviation. And after that I returned to Poloznik.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: So it was a fact that this large group -- sorry, this large number of people you were in were indeed stopped by shelling and stopped -- and shooting, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: SUHRA SINANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Stopped for going to Bjelovac and -- including you, stopped from getting food or properties, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: SUHRA SINANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Can I -- can I take it, given your testimony, that you rather get killed than return without food to Srebrenica? Did you at least tried once more to get to Bjelovac?

utterances.speaker: SUHRA SINANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, when I returned on that occasion to Poloznik, I didn't know whether I would be hit by a shell or by the planes. I didn't know whether I would die there or reach Poloznik alive.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: What I mean is -- and let me be clear with it. I don't want to have you misunderstanding. I know the tragedies during wartime, but I try to understand. You were very -- verifies in stating to the Court: I rather get killed than return empty-handed to my family. And later on, I rather get a bullet than return without food. So I tried to understand you in such a desperate situation that no cost you will get that food. And please explain to me that you indeed tried once more and more again, because that should be the outcome of such a statement. Can you explain, please.

utterances.speaker: SUHRA SINANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, naturally I wanted to get there; that was my wish. But due to the very intense shelling, we were unable to get there.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: I move to another issue. You met in Loznica you met Mira Filipovic, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: SUHRA SINANOVIC
utterances.text: No, not in Loznica but rather in Poloznik.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Poloznik. I apologise. Thank you for this correction. Was her husband with her when she arrived at Poloznik?

utterances.speaker: SUHRA SINANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: And what was her attitude? Was she at ease or did -- was she frightened? Can you tell us?

utterances.speaker: SUHRA SINANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, no, she was not relaxed, exactly. The two of us talked and her attitude was - how should I put it? - rather normal, fairly normal. She was not too scared.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Her son was wounded, isn't she -- isn't it?

utterances.speaker: SUHRA SINANOVIC
utterances.text: No, no. The Brano boy was wounded.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Did she tell -- did she also tell you where her husband was?

utterances.speaker: SUHRA SINANOVIC
utterances.text: She didn't say anything about her husband. I know nothing about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Didn't she -- did she tell you that her husband didn't knew where she was at the moment?

utterances.speaker: SUHRA SINANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Did you learn later on, I mean after all these events, after you returned to Srebrenica in the years after, did you learn later on a rumour that Mira jumped in the river Drina and -- as well as her children, something like that? A rumour?

utterances.speaker: SUHRA SINANOVIC
utterances.text: No. I was with Mira in Poloznik the entire night.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: No. I mean afterwards. After you met Mira and then later on you went to Srebrenica. In the years after, did you find out as well because you met her and you know that she was in Poloznik, but that there was also a rumour that she jumped into the river Drina?

utterances.speaker: SUHRA SINANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: I would like to move to that house where you were in together with Mira. Was it in the centre of Poloznik or in the -- in the neighbourhood of the centre? Can you tell us?

utterances.speaker: SUHRA SINANOVIC
utterances.text: In the centre of Poloznik.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: I will show you a map.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, I have a map prepared to show to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Your Honour, I just have one issue with this map. I'm sure Your Honours would point it out in any event. There's a date on the map and obviously --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let me see it before then. One moment before you give it to the --

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: My learned friend means the date in the middle, under.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes. It's simply this: That I don't want it to be suggested to this witness that this map necessarily represents the state of roads, et cetera, in 1992. There's a date, obviously a later date, and I wouldn't want the witness to be confused by thinking that this necessarily depicts the situation in 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: We can, we can --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Fair enough. I think that's fair enough and she had heard what you've said.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Your Honours, we can be frank about that and transparent to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: This is a map from that date.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: And then I will ask something about what she knows.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, go ahead. It's no big deal, actually. We can -- yes. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Witness, you see the map in front of you. Can you point out the village that you were in, Poloznik, where you met Mira Filipovic?

utterances.speaker: SUHRA SINANOVIC
utterances.text: It's here.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: It's not so clear on my monitor, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: She found it. All right.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Poloznik.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Can you please encircle it with one of the pencils.

utterances.speaker: SUHRA SINANOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Can you also track the village of Pirici?

utterances.speaker: SUHRA SINANOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Is it correct that from Pirici towards the Drina River there is a road? Can you confirm that, to your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: SUHRA SINANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please repeat the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: My question is: Can you confirm that in your knowledge there is a road from Pirici towards the Drina River, towards the main road, Bratunac-Skelani?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Again, is that on the map or at the same period of time? That's what I don't follow.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: To your -- to her knowledge. The next question will be time frame.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The road to Pirici was also narrow, and the road to Loznicka Rijeka. Up until -- from Loznicka Rijeka to Bratunac there was a real road, whereas the other one was just a dirt road.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Now, is this road from Pirici towards the road Bratunac-Skelani, this main road along the Drina River?

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: I'm leading now, I'm aware of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: That road from Pirici towards that main road that I mentioned, is that a broader road?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Than what?

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Broader than the road Poloznik-Pirici?

utterances.speaker: SUHRA SINANOVIC
utterances.text: No. These are also narrow village roads.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Now, what do you mean by "narrow village roads"? From Pirici towards that main road, how broad is that in your estimation? Can you give that in metres or ...

utterances.speaker: SUHRA SINANOVIC
utterances.text: As I said last time, this is a goat path for pedestrians. That's the kind of road it was. It was less than a metre wide.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: But you testified in that respect regarding the road Poloznik-Pirici. But now I only ask for the road from Pirici towards that main road that leads to Bratunac. Is that a metre broad in your testimony as well or broader?

utterances.speaker: SUHRA SINANOVIC
utterances.text: From Pirici to Loznicka Rijeka, the road is as I've described. And from Loznicka Rijeka to Bratunac there is an asphalt road.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Yes. But is there a road from the main road to Pirici, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: SUHRA SINANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: So for the villages of Poloznik-Pirici there is no road to come to the main road from Bratunac to Skelani?

utterances.speaker: SUHRA SINANOVIC
utterances.text: There is no proper road, as I told you. These roads are narrow village roads meant for pedestrians only.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Has there ever been a road in the past from the main road up to Pirici, other than a pedestrian road?

utterances.speaker: SUHRA SINANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Thank you for that exhibit. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Please bear me a moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Will you please give it a exhibit number, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: I want to tender it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: This will become Prosecution Exhibit P5 --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: P576, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: 76. Thank you. Yes, yes, Judge Eser.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: I am still a little bit confused, Mrs. Sinanovic. When we have the map in front of us, there's a road on the map going from the road Bjelovac-Skelani to Pirici and it's clearly lined in the map. And there seems to be a connection between Pirici and Poloznik. Now, is this the same road? Is it possible to go by a car from Bjelovac to Pirici? Even if it is not an asphalt road, is it possible to go by car from Bjelovac to Pirici?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Again, is this December 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: This is why Mr. Jones pointed out the date of this map, because this may be misleading. The situation as it was in 1992, and we are concentrating on 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: And I submit that she -- she even stated that there never has been a road ever at any time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's her testimony. I mean, I'm not questioning her testimony or commenting on it of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, just at the last [inaudible] Mr. Wubben, he said has there ever in the past, which was -- certainly for my part, I wouldn't understand that to mean at this moment right now there is no such road.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I'm not saying there is.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: That was his comment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But I'm not commenting, of course. The only thing is, if I may add on what Judge Eser has pointed out, did the people, to your knowledge, the people in Pirici, did they own cars? Did they --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Did they have tractors?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Were they engaged in agriculture mainly?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, agriculture, but they were using ox-carts and horses to work the land.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yeah, but then after having worked the land and taken up the produce and collected the produce, would they sell it outside of Pirici or not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So the people of Pirici were literally in 1992 cut off completely from the rest of -- of the area in a sense that none of them could travel by car? There was no way you could get into or out of the village of Pirici by car?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It's -- I don't think we could have it more clear than that. I'm sorry for having -- but, basically, I was picking up on what you were obviously trying to -- but this is what I had understood from the very beginning, basically, but I just wanted her to explain it better. Yes, Mr. Wubben.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: And in addition -- and in addition then of the questions by --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Perhaps if, usher, you could ask the witness to sign her name at the top right-hand corner of the map in the white part, please, on the white margin.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I'm sorry for having interrupted you, Mr. Wubben. I thank you, Madam. Yes, Mr. Wubben.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: To sum up, is it then your testimony that there is no road now nor has there ever been a road from Pirici towards the main road?

utterances.speaker: SUHRA SINANOVIC
utterances.text: No, there never was a road before, and as for now I don't know. Most likely there isn't one.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Thank you. I return to the town of Srebrenica. You've been there from June 1992. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SUHRA SINANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: You stated that you didn't notice any police. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: SUHRA SINANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: So during the time from June, and I know that there was this interruption of this journey in December, but from June you didn't see any policemen at all in the streets of Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: SUHRA SINANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Does that mean you did saw or the confirmation that you didn't saw?

utterances.speaker: SUHRA SINANOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't see.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: You didn't see. Are you familiar a building called the SUP building in Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: SUHRA SINANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: One moment, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: You state you didn't saw any policemen. Did you saw any persons in uniform in Srebrenica at the time, from June 1992?

utterances.speaker: SUHRA SINANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Does that also include that you didn't saw any soldiers, any fighters in uniforms?

utterances.speaker: SUHRA SINANOVIC
utterances.text: That confirms that I didn't see them.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Did you saw any person from that time from June 1992 wearing any arms in Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: SUHRA SINANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Did you ever heard of a person called Naser Oric at the time?

utterances.speaker: SUHRA SINANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: You stayed there from June 1992 until what year and month in Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: SUHRA SINANOVIC
utterances.text: Until the fall of Srebrenica in 1995, on the 11th of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: So it is your testimony that from June 1992 until 1995 you didn't hear about the person called Naser Oric. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SUHRA SINANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Did you hear of a name of Zulfo Tursunovic?

utterances.speaker: SUHRA SINANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: And meaning also during that period of time, 1992/1995, is that correct, you didn't learn about this person?

utterances.speaker: SUHRA SINANOVIC
utterances.text: I said "no."

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Did you heard about a person called Akif Ustic at the time?

utterances.speaker: SUHRA SINANOVIC
utterances.text: No. I was a refugee from Bratunac, so I know none of these people.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: But you confirmed that you didn't know of those people that I mentioned, that also never heard of them, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: SUHRA SINANOVIC
utterances.text: That's right. I'm confirming that I never heard of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Please bear me a moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, certainly, Mr. Wubben.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: About the person Slavoljub Filipovic, your former neighbour. You testified about him that you knew him as being a hooligan, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: SUHRA SINANOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't say that he was a hooligan. He was just a person who liked provoking incidents while we went to school.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: And this very person also moved into your property, setting up a cafe, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: SUHRA SINANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Doesn't that make you angry about him?

utterances.speaker: SUHRA SINANOVIC
utterances.text: Naturally I am angry. Why would I give my property to somebody else and not be angry about it?

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Please bear me a moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: And about her -- about his wife, Mira Filipovic. You returned -- upon your return in Srebrenica, did you ever learned that Mira has been captured and held prisoned in Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: SUHRA SINANOVIC
utterances.text: No. When I was with her, that was the occasion when I saw her and then I never heard anything else about her afterwards.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: That was my last question, Your Honour. That finalised my cross.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Mr. Wubben. Is there re-examination, Mr. Jones?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes, just a few, brief questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Take your time. We have three-quarters of an hour.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And I assure you we are not going to fill all of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Ms. Sinanovic, going back to April 1992 you were asked about village guards and you said you also saw soldiers during the daytime, Serb soldiers. Now, when you saw them during the daytime in Bjelovac, were they guarding anything?

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I protest. She -- she was referring to village guards and not connecting the issue of guarding towards the soldiers in her testimony. And this suggestion goes too far, this guiding the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Go ahead, Mr. Jones. Village guard automatically implies that they are there to guard something or someone.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes, precisely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Particularly the village.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Your Honour, with all respect, but village guards can be civilians who act as guards.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: But that's different from a soldier in an army.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: That's precisely my question. In fact, that's what I'm getting at, whether the soldiers were actually doing any guarding, the soldiers she saw during the day, never mind any civilians.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: She said village guards and that she saw soldiers during the daytime and that they were Serb, of Serb nationality. Now, the question is: "Now, when you saw them during the daytime in Bjelovac, were they guarding anything?" What's wrong with that question? What were they -- basically, you can also ask her directly when she saw these soldiers or these village guards, what they were doing according to her.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: That's fine with me.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I'll ask that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes, the soldiers, by that I mean people in uniforms with weapons that you saw during the day, what were they doing?

utterances.speaker: SUHRA SINANOVIC
utterances.text: I saw those soldiers. They walked down the street next to my house and they went in the direction of the school. The school was at a distance of about 50 metres by my house. I didn't know those people. I didn't say that they were on guard that day; I just saw them walk by, walk down the street. And they went in the direction of the school.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Right. So you said you didn't know them. Do I take it from that that they weren't from Bjelovac?

utterances.speaker: SUHRA SINANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did not know them.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And I think it's fair enough for me to ask the question: Did they appear to be guarding anything?

utterances.speaker: SUHRA SINANOVIC
utterances.text: Perhaps -- well, I don't know how to answer that question. If you see a uniformed soldier, I mean, what else is he supposed to do?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Now, you mentioned when you were at Cvijeta Ilic's house you saw Novo Ilic. Remind us what he was wearing and whether he was armed.

utterances.speaker: SUHRA SINANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. He was wearing an olive-drab uniform and he was carrying a rifle when I saw him, when I saw them, actually, Slavoljub and him.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, just a very important correction. The witness did not say in her reply that when she saw uniformed men, what else, what other things, they were supposed to do, but what are they meant to do. Because we feel it would change the significance and the meaning of her statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Let's proceed, Mr. Jones.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we have that clarified?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I don't think we need to, Mr. Jones, let's go ahead. Proceed. It doesn't make a difference in the minds in fact Trial Chamber, so proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: To summarise, when you were at Cvijeta Ilic's, you saw Novo Ilic in uniform and with a weapon, you saw Slavoljub Filipovic in uniform with a weapon. Did you see any other Serbs in the vicinity of that house who were uniformed and armed?

utterances.speaker: SUHRA SINANOVIC
utterances.text: Not on that evening.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: On some other evening?

utterances.speaker: SUHRA SINANOVIC
utterances.text: I saw the teacher, Sarac, beforehand, and the others when they got there, and the soldiers who went down the street.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Right. Now, you were asked about village guards. You've referred to these people, Novo Ilic, Slavoljub Filipovic, Sarac. When you spoke -- you agreed they were guards, were you referring to those people or did you have other people in mind?

utterances.speaker: SUHRA SINANOVIC
utterances.text: I said that because his mother, Cvijeta, told me that we should get out of the house for five minute and stay in the darkness out there because they wanted to go and do their guard duty; that's what I said. She said that we should get out of their way for five minutes and give them time to leave and take up their guard duty.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: All right. And finally, let me put it this way: Did you in Bjelovac in April and May 1992 see anyone in civilian clothes who you would describe as a village guard?

utterances.speaker: SUHRA SINANOVIC
utterances.text: If it's a village guard, as far as I'm concerned I don't know who that could be keeping guard in civilian clothes because I did not go out of my own house to go observing any other people or checking on anyone's movements. I mean, how could I describe that? How could I see that?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: All right. So I mean, for you the village guard that you saw were uniformed and armed. Would that be correct?

utterances.speaker: SUHRA SINANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you. You were also asked about whether you saw any trenches, I think it was, in Bjelovac and you said no. Do you know a place called Podbrdje?

utterances.speaker: SUHRA SINANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Did you ever see any sort of fortification there in April, May 1992?

utterances.speaker: SUHRA SINANOVIC
utterances.text: I saw it when I went to see my parents in Bratunac on the 11th of May, in the morning of that day. A day or two earlier I also went to Bratunac because my parents were ill, and there was a kind of checkpoint where we were asked to show our IDs. And there was a kind of shelter there. And on the 11th of May when I set out, there were sacks all along this road. There was a kind of shelter built for those soldiers, the entire lane.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: All right. I actually heard the word "bunker" in Bosnian. Did you use the word "bunker" or did you say shelter?

utterances.speaker: SUHRA SINANOVIC
utterances.text: Bunker.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And who was manning this bunker, to your knowledge, Serbs or Muslims?

utterances.speaker: SUHRA SINANOVIC
utterances.text: Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: All right. Now, moving on to 14th of December, 1992, it was -- will you accept it that you and your -- the group you were with were stopped or prevented by shelling from getting into Bjelovac. You also mentioned earlier in your testimony that other groups were going to other places like Brezovica. So my question is: Was yours the only group of civilians trying to get into Bjelovac, to your knowledge, or were the people -- the groups in the broader area also moving around?

utterances.speaker: SUHRA SINANOVIC
utterances.text: In the broader area.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And were you aware at that stage of people going to Voljavica and Zaluzje, some of those places?

utterances.speaker: SUHRA SINANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, because they just went looking for food.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Now, you told us how you tried to get to Bjelovac on the 14th of December, 1992, and that you actually got there on the 20th to the 21st of December, 1992. Now, what were you doing in that period in between? Were you simply resting in Poloznik or were you trying to get into Bjelovac?

utterances.speaker: SUHRA SINANOVIC
utterances.text: I was trying to get in. How could I consider resting, hungry as I was?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: So were you trying to get in every day, into Bjelovac, in that period?

utterances.speaker: SUHRA SINANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, but because of all the shelling and aviation, as I said, I was unable to.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Right. Now, dealing with Poloznik and access to Poloznik. Was it possible to get from - and I'm including Pirici as well - Pirici, Poloznik down to the Drina on ox or on horse on the path that you've described?

utterances.speaker: SUHRA SINANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, on horseback between Poloznik and Pirici.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And from Pirici down to the Drina, were people able to pass from there; and if so, how?

utterances.speaker: SUHRA SINANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you repeat the question, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes. How did people get from Pirici down to Loznicka Rijeka and the Drina?

utterances.speaker: SUHRA SINANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you mean on that day, on the 14th or what?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: No. My apologies for being unclear. Before the war.

utterances.speaker: SUHRA SINANOVIC
utterances.text: That's what they did before the war, on horseback.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Rite. So it's not the case that Pirici and Poloznik were completely cut off from the rest of the world, is it?

utterances.speaker: SUHRA SINANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Do you know if people - and only if you know - but whether the people in Pirici and Poloznik worked outside of those villages? In other words, if they travelled to a town and had jobs there, if that's something you know about?

utterances.speaker: SUHRA SINANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Most people worked at the Sase mine in Bratunac, but they walked to Loznicka Rijeka and then got on the bus and travelled in the direction of wherever they job -- their job was.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. I can see I think you're getting tired. And I just have four or five questions so if you'll bear with me, Ms. Sinanovic. On this subject, it might seem strange to us in the West to think of a village which has no access by car. Is that unusual in Eastern Bosnia in 1992 or is that something which did occur?

utterances.speaker: SUHRA SINANOVIC
utterances.text: It did exist. What I said is the truth. Not a single family in Poloznik or in Pirici owned a car; they didn't even have their driver's license because they didn't need it because they couldn't have accessed their homes by car. And Poloznik and Pirici are both at a fairly high altitude.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Okay. Now, you were asked about whether you knew the SUP building in Srebrenica. You also told us that you -- you're from Bratunac municipality. Did you actually visit Srebrenica, the town, much before the war?

utterances.speaker: SUHRA SINANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Sorry. I have another question. I'm going back to Pirici and Poloznik for one moment. When did you leave the Srebrenica-Bratunac area?

utterances.speaker: SUHRA SINANOVIC
utterances.text: I left the Bratunac area -- or rather, I left the Bjelovac on the 11th of May and I was in Poloznik until the morning of the 2nd of June. On the 2nd of June I set off in the direction of Srebrenica and the journey took about 24 hours until we got to Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes. Sorry. It's my fault. I should have been -- made it clearer. After the fall of Srebrenica in July 1995, did you -- did you return to live in either the Srebrenica or Bratunac municipalities?

utterances.speaker: SUHRA SINANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Have you been back to visit that area much in the last ten years?

utterances.speaker: SUHRA SINANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. First I went to my place, Bjelovac, on the 4th of August, 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Right. But as far as whether there's a road or not between Pirici and the Bratunac-Skelani road, is that something you've actually been able to verify for yourself in the last ten years or not?

utterances.speaker: SUHRA SINANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: It was also put to you and you accepted that to a certain extent you were angry with Slavoljub Filipovic for taking your property. Has that affected your testimony about him today in any way?

utterances.speaker: SUHRA SINANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Have you given truthful testimony about him today?

utterances.speaker: SUHRA SINANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Are you angry against Mira Filipovic?

utterances.speaker: SUHRA SINANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Are you angry against Slavka Matic?

utterances.speaker: SUHRA SINANOVIC
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Mr. Jones. Judge Brydensholt has -- yes, one moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Sorry, her "no" wasn't interpreted for Slavka Matic.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Would you repeat your answer, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I notice that now, too. For the record I heard her say "no." Yes, let's proceed. Yes, Judge Brydensholt.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BRYDENSHOLT
utterances.text: On the 14th of December, 1992, when you were asked to go to this cellar where Mira Filipovic was, what did she say to you when you arrived, do you remember? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: SUHRA SINANOVIC
utterances.text: She wasn't in the cellar; she was on the ground floor. We talked nicely and she told me that Rosa Ilic and the Ilic family in general collected my belongings from my house, my property.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BRYDENSHOLT
utterances.text: Did she give any explanation why she was found where you found her?

utterances.speaker: SUHRA SINANOVIC
utterances.text: No. She didn't mention anything.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BRYDENSHOLT
utterances.text: Were you very surprised when you saw her? She was not a Muslim and I guess you were very surprised?

utterances.speaker: SUHRA SINANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Well, I did say that that man said to me, Okay, since you're neighbours, you knew one another and she had been working at the mine as a cook, that it would be a good idea for me to sit with her so as for her not to be disturbed by anyone and for me to take care of the children during the night and everything. And she didn't say anything much. At first we talked to each other. We exchanged some views, and then she lied down and tried to get some sleep.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BRYDENSHOLT
utterances.text: She was not crying in any way?

utterances.speaker: SUHRA SINANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BRYDENSHOLT
utterances.text: When you returned to Srebrenica after the 20th or 21st, didn't you hear anything about what had happened to Mira?

utterances.speaker: SUHRA SINANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BRYDENSHOLT
utterances.text: Well, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Judge Brydensholt. Judge Eser, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: I also would like to come back to the 13th or 14th of December. You told us that more than thousand people have been on the way in the direction to Bjelovac. Now, my question is: In the same period of time do you know whether there was on some other day a lot of people, thousands of people, would go to Bjelovac? Or was it only on the 13th or 14th of December that thousands of people would go to the direction of Bjelovac.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I think she said to Poloznik.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: Poloznik. I said direction of Bjelovac. I mean, Bjelovac, if you look at the map, is not far away from Poloznik. Let's say Bjelovac, Poloznik, Pirici --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let me intervene a little bit.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: It has to be precise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: There is a part, there is a part in the testimony where certainly she is being referred then to her movement towards Bjelovac and she is roughly indicating that she intended -- was trying to get to Bjelovac and she didn't succeed. And then a question was put to her because she mentioned a group and she said there was quite a number or something like that, and she was asked what that number was like and she said it was thousand, thousands, thousands.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: It's something that is a very important issue for us, and if the witness speaks about thousands going in the direction of Poloznik, which I don't agree is on the direction to Bjelovac, I don't want it suggested to her that thousands of people went to Bjelovac. That's not her testimony and we can check in the transcript whether she ever said that thousands of people on the same day all headed towards Bjelovac. I'm sure she didn't say that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment. Let me find it. Roughly -- not roughly, we are on page 63 and 64. Now, we go to page 63, line 21 and the question was: "But I take it then that the whole group hide for the shelling" -- forgive me for reading the transcript as it is. "Or how many, by the way? I rephrase the question. How many people were there aiming for Bjelovac with you?" The answer: "Do you mean the 14th?" "Q. Yes, yes. "A. It was a large group and whoever was able to find shelter under the trees did that. Others just stood on the goat path expecting to be hit and killed. "Q. Can you give a number in that respect, hundreds, hundreds of people in that group? "A. Thousands, not hundreds." So, definitely, this answer, as to whether it's correct or not is another number. But definitely the answer of thousands was in relation to a previous question that referred her to her attempt to reach Bjelovac together with others.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes, she's trying to get to Bjelovac. There are thousands of people are in Poloznik. It's wrong to say that there were thousands going towards Bjelovac.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Stop here, now, for the time being, because I think the discussion has gone a little bit too far in the presence of the witness now. Please repeat your question, Judge Eser. Sorry for having interrupted you, but -- I got your point, Mr. Jones, but I think you have to concede that when she said thousands she was answering a question more or less as to what was the situation where she was trying to head towards Bjelovac. So let's get Judge Eser's question again. I don't see it on my screen so I have to get back a page or two. "Judge Eser: Now, my question is: In the same period of time do you know whether there was on some other day a lot of people, thousands of people, would go to Bjelovac? Or was it only on the 13th or 14th of December that thousands of people would go to the direction of Bjelovac?" So now she can answer the question. If -- if you believe that what is being suggested to you that on the 14th there weren't thousands of people going to Bjelovac, please say so, but do try to answer the question. Also, which basically asks from you whether you are aware that there may have been other days on which people tried -- or thousands tried to reach Bjelovac.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: Or the area of Bjelovac. I was saying in the direction of Bjelovac instead of going to Zvornik or Fakovici or somewhere else. The question was --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: -- the broad direction of Bjelovac including some other villages like Voljevica or Pirici or Poloznik. That was my question. Whether only on the 13th or 14th there was a big group of people going towards this area or whether there have been other days where a similar great group of people would go in the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: In the same direction.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: -- same direction.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Which includes Voljevica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Now it's definitely a broader area than the town of Bjelovac itself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: Does the question -- do you -- could you please answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: She may still be receiving interpretation; I don't know.

utterances.speaker: SUHRA SINANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please repeat the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: So my question is: You told us that on the 13th or 14th, at least in these two days, there has been a lot of people, more than thousands of people, were moving into the broader area of Bjelovac, not only to the city of Bjelovac, town of Bjelovac, but also the neighbouring --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Surrounding places.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: -- surrounding villages. Now my question is whether it was only on these days that such a large group of people would move in this direction or whether also on other days before the 13th or after the 13th you had a big movement of people going into this direction? That's my question. I think it's not so difficult to answer.

utterances.speaker: SUHRA SINANOVIC
utterances.text: On other days as well. There would be people trying to get to Bjelovac, Zaluzje, and Voljevica to get some kind of food. Large groups of people would be setting off after the 14th of December.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: So large groups, more than thousands of people?

utterances.speaker: SUHRA SINANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: But did you see by your own eyes that these people -- such large groups of people would go to this direction?

utterances.speaker: SUHRA SINANOVIC
utterances.text: No. I don't mean thousands or more than a thousand people. What I mean is larger groups, hundreds of people or so. I didn't actually say more than a thousand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: I think you have -- I remember that you said more than thousand people, but at --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Anyway.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: -- any rate, on other days the groups have been smaller than on the 13th and 14th. I have no further questions. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Madam Sinanovic, I don't have any questions for you, which means that your testimony comes to an end here. On behalf of the Tribunal, but particularly on behalf of Judge Brydensholt, Judge Eser, and on my own behalf I should like to thank you for having accepted to come over and give testimony as a Defence witness. You will now be escorted out of the courtroom by Madam Usher and other members of our staff will extend to you all their -- the help and assistance that you require to facilitate your return back home at the earliest possible. Once more, I thank you. And on behalf of everyone, I wish you a safe journey back home.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Jones, I inquired with a member of the registry -- you may remain seated. It's okay. A member of the registry about that matter about the practice that they have adopted in the past.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And since I am not aware of who you have in mind, obviously, and whether you have in mind of having the examination, the tests, carried out here in the Netherlands or outside of the Netherlands, I did alert them to that possibility. So if that is not the case, please tell me because it will -- it will facilitate matters. Because in the other cases, obviously, they did not have this problem to -- to deal with.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes. It would be a question of examination outside the Netherlands.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Outside the Netherlands.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And using his own equipment. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. And therefore, Mr. Wubben, you also need -- because as I explained earlier we definitely -- and for the time being at least we definitely see a difference between documents which are exhibits and therefore within the jurisdiction of the Trial Chamber with the accompanying relative responsibility of the registrar and documents which are the exclusive property of the Prosecution for which the Trial Chamber is not for the time being responsible, and neither is the registrar.
